name: Babylonians
also_known_as: Chaldeans (the ruling tribe of the Neo-Babylonian empire)
summary: The people of Babylon on the Euphrates, the city where humanity built the tower of Babel. Under Nebuchadnezzar and the Chaldean dynasty they destroyed Jerusalem and Solomon's Temple and carried Judah into seventy years of exile — the setting of Daniel's furnace and lions' den. In Revelation, 'Babylon' becomes the name for the whole proud world system set against God.
name_meaning: Babylonian Bab-ili, 'gate of god'. Genesis plays on the Hebrew balal, 'to confuse': 'Therefore is the name of it called Babel; because the LORD did there confound the language.'

origin.account: Nimrod, son of Cush, 'a mighty hunter before the LORD', began his kingdom at 'Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar'. There, after the flood, humanity built a city and tower 'whose top may reach unto heaven', and God scattered them by confusing their language. The Chaldeans (Kasdim) were Aramaic-related tribes of southern Mesopotamia. Abram's family came from 'Ur of the Chaldees', and a Chaldean dynasty ruled the Neo-Babylonian empire (626–539 BC).

lineage.ancestor: Nimrod (founder of Babel), son of Cush; Chaldeans possibly from Chesed, son of Nahor
lineage.notes: Genesis links Babel's founding to Nimrod of Ham's line. The Chaldean name (Kasdim) is often linked to Chesed, a nephew of Abraham, and Abraham's own family came from 'Ur of the Chaldees'. The Babylonians were therefore a mixed Sumerian, Akkadian, Amorite, Kassite and Chaldean population.

homeland.region: Babylonia (Shinar, 'the land of the Chaldeans') — southern Mesopotamia
homeland.description: The flat, irrigated alluvial plain between the lower Euphrates and Tigris, south of modern Baghdad down to the Persian Gulf marshes. It was intensely fertile when canals were maintained — 'by the rivers of Babylon'. The city of Babylon was rebuilt by Nebuchadnezzar with the Ishtar Gate, the Processional Way and the great ziggurat Etemenanki.

places.name: Babylon
places.note: 'Is not this great Babylon, that I have built?'

places.name: River Chebar
places.note: Where Ezekiel saw his visions among the exiles.

timeline.event: The tower of Babel; languages confused and peoples scattered.
Amraphel king of Shinar raids Canaan with Chedorlaomer; Abram rescues Lot.
Hammurabi makes Babylon a great power and issues his law code (Old Babylonian period).
Merodach-baladan sends envoys to Hezekiah; Isaiah foretells the exile to Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar defeats Egypt at Carchemish and takes Daniel and other young nobles to Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar takes Jerusalem, deports King Jehoiachin, Ezekiel and 10,000 captives, and installs Zedekiah.
After Zedekiah's revolt, Jerusalem and the Temple are burned; Judah is carried away.
Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego survive the fiery furnace; Nebuchadnezzar is humbled by madness and praises the Most High.
Evil-merodach releases Jehoiachin from prison and gives him a place at the king's table.
Belshazzar's feast; the writing on the wall; Babylon falls to the Medes and Persians that night.
Peter writes from 'Babylon' (probably a code name for Rome). Revelation describes the fall of 'Babylon the great'.

religion.practices: State religion centred on Marduk's temple Esagila and its ziggurat. It included astrology, divination and a class of 'magicians, astrologers, sorcerers, and Chaldeans', whom Daniel outshone. The prophets mocked idols carried on animals' backs.

importance: Babylon is the other great pole of the Bible's geography after Jerusalem. Babel stands for human pride trying to reach heaven without God. The Babylonian exile was the great crisis of the Old Testament: the Temple destroyed and the Davidic throne vacant. It purged Judah of idolatry and produced Daniel, Ezekiel, Lamentations and the hope of return after seventy years. Jeremiah told the exiles to 'seek the peace of the city' where they were carried. In Revelation, Babylon becomes the city of man opposed to the city of God.

impact.how: Taken as youths, renamed Belteshazzar, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, and tested for their faith in the king's court.
Preached submission to Babylon, was accused of treason, and was freed by the Babylonians.
A priest in exile who received visions of God's glory leaving and returning to the Temple.
Saw his sons killed and was blinded and taken to Babylon.
Wept by the rivers of Babylon, but were told to build, plant and pray for the city.

notable_people.name: Nebuzar-adan
notable_people.role: Captain of the guard who burned Jerusalem

notable_people.name: Belshazzar
notable_people.role: Last ruler in Babylon, slain the night it fell

key_verses.text: Therefore is the name of it called Babel; because the LORD did there confound the language of all the earth: and from thence did the LORD scatter them abroad upon the face of all the earth.
And he burnt the house of the LORD, and the king’s house, and all the houses of Jerusalem, and every great man’s house burnt he with fire.
By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yea, we wept, when we remembered Zion.
And seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the LORD for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace.
For thus saith the LORD, That after seventy years be accomplished at Babylon I will visit you, and perform my good word toward you, in causing you to return to this place.
If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king.

fate.summary: Cyrus the Persian took Babylon in 539 BC, largely without a fight, as Isaiah had foretold by name. Babylon remained a major city under Persia and Alexander (who died there in 323 BC). It declined after the Seleucids founded Seleucia on the Tigris, and was largely deserted by the early centuries AD, as Isaiah and Jeremiah had said it would become 'desolations'.

today.summary: No people today are called Babylonians; the population of the region is Iraqi. The ruins of Babylon, near Hillah, became a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2019. The name 'Chaldean' lives on in the Chaldean Catholic Church, whose Aramaic-speaking members take it as an ethnic identity. The Babylonian Jewish community, which stayed after the exile, produced the Babylonian Talmud and survived in Iraq for 2,600 years until most Iraqi Jews left in 1950–1951.
today.descendants: Absorbed into the population of Iraq; Chaldean and Assyrian Christians and Iraqi Jews all have roots there.
today.modern_legacy: The Ishtar Gate (reconstructed in Berlin's Pergamon Museum), the 60-minute hour and 360-degree circle from Babylonian mathematics, and 'Babel' and 'Babylon' as words for confusion and decadence.

archaeology.name: Babylonian Chronicle ABC 5 ('Jerusalem Chronicle')
archaeology.significance: Records Nebuchadnezzar capturing 'the city of Judah' on 2 Adar (16 March 597 BC) and appointing a king of his choice.

archaeology.name: Jehoiachin ration tablets
archaeology.significance: List oil rations for 'Ya'ukin king of the land of Yahud' and his sons.

archaeology.name: Nabonidus Cylinder from Ur
archaeology.significance: Names Belshazzar as Nabonidus' eldest son — explaining why Daniel could only be 'third ruler' in the kingdom.
